title: Choose DoseGuard's new world
question: The roll assigned Sun Print, the blue-and-white cyanotype of a healing plant. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: Sun Print
options.lineage: Victorian cyanotypes of medicinal plants, printed by sunlight on blue paper
options.thesis: Your dose is a sun print: the pills show as white shapes on soft blue, and each safety check develops the print a little deeper until it is fixed.
options.viewport: Pale blue shell with Today and Setup tabs and STOP; the dose due now is one large blue print showing its pills as white shapes, with Take my dose under it and the rest of the day as a short list beside it.
options.risk: Cyanotype is a niche word; the healing feel depends on the plant prints staying quiet and the blue staying light.

raised.raise: STOP, Cancel and Reset always sit alone with empty space around them, never next to everyday buttons.
Pill colours appear only inside the dose print; everything else stays blue and white.
One thing is ringed on any screen: the thing you can do right now.
The dose due now swells to own the screen; everything else steps back to its edge.
State lives in form as well as words: done is solid, waiting is dashed, cancelled is struck through.

options.label: Morning Sky
options.lineage: the sky outside your window from dawn to night
options.thesis: Your day is a sky: doses sit on the sun's arc, the screen brightens and dims with the time of day, and the next dose is where the sun is now.
options.viewport: A wide sky band across the top with the sun's arc and today's doses on it; below, the due dose large and calm with Take my dose; Setup behind one door.
options.risk: Sky and sun is a familiar wellness look, and the gradient must never lower text contrast.

options.label: Ticket Wallet
options.lineage: jet-age airline ticket wallets with carbon coupons
options.thesis: Each dose is a ticket book: one coupon per safety step tears off in order, and the wallet always shows what is left.
options.viewport: Today shows the due dose as a ticket with its time and pills; Take my dose opens a coupon book where each check stamps and tears off.
options.case: Fuses cleanly: steps map to coupons and stamped states keep released, collected and taken explicit; less healing, since travel reads as stress.
options.risk: Can drift back toward the old label-and-sticker look if stamps get loud.

options.label: Garden Guide Map
options.thesis: Areas as swelling lobes of flat colour.
options.case: Fuses poorly: playful and green, it breaks the blue-and-white brand and reads as a children's map.

options.label: Dark Console
options.case: Fuses poorly: dark and technical, the opposite of calm for an anxious person at home.
options.kept: Dangerous actions sit alone with empty space around them.

options.label: Lexicon Page
options.thesis: Black text columns with colour quarantined in plates.
options.viewport: A dense two-column page with guide words.
options.case: Fuses poorly: dense reading text and cream stock fight large type and the blue brand.
options.risk: Too dense for a daily glance.
options.kept: Colour only inside the plate that carries meaning.

options.label: Star Atlas
options.thesis: Importance as dot size on a navy sky.
options.viewport: Doses as stars on a night chart.
options.case: Fuses poorly: a night chart is beautiful but hard to read at a glance in the morning.
options.kept: Only the thing under your eye is ringed.

options.label: Emission Rail
options.thesis: State as line height, dash and doubling on charcoal.
options.viewport: Every destination a tick on one rail.
options.case: Fuses poorly: abstract and dark; a person in pain should not decode lines.
options.kept: State is carried by form, not colour alone.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A clean medication app: white cards, a blue accent, a list of today's pills, played straight at full craft.
canonCard.viewport: Greeting, a timeline of today's doses as cards, the due one highlighted with Take now.
canonCard.risk: Looks like every pill-reminder app by design.
